paragraphs: My name is Tom, and I am twelve years old. I am awake at six o'clock every school day. I eat breakfast, and I leave home at seven. I take my bag, my books, and my lunch box. My school has more than a thousand students. We have seven lessons in a day. Teacher Nick gives our class a paper for the week. It says which subject comes in each lesson. The first lesson starts at eight o'clock.

The first lesson is math. The second lesson is English at nine o'clock. The third lesson is science at ten o'clock. Teacher Nick explains the sun and the moon. "Why does the moon change its shape?" asks Hugo. Teacher Nick explains with a ball and a lamp. We write the answers in our notebooks. The fourth lesson is geography at eleven o'clock. Then we have lunch at twelve o'clock.

In the afternoon, the fifth lesson is art. It starts at one o'clock. The sixth lesson is gym at two o'clock. Coach Matt is our gym teacher. Gym is my favorite subject, so I am never tired in that lesson. Ben is the first boy to run, and I am the second. We run around the field two times. The seventh lesson is music at three o'clock.

School ends at four o'clock. "Which lesson is your favorite?" asks Ben. "The sixth one," I say. "I like the seventh one," says Ben. "Music is fun, and I can sing." We walk home together. Number words help us say the order of the day. First, second, third, and so on.
text.summary: Tom tells the order of his seven lessons in a school day. Each lesson has an ordinal number and a time written as words.
